title: Transactional model swap and forensic snapshot playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes a transactional, auditable process for swapping model binaries in private deployments (VPC / on-prem) while capturing deterministic forensic snapshots and evidence artifacts. The goal is to allow a safe, reversible model refresh that: (1) preserves inference continuity, (2) provides court-ready evidence for compliance reviews, and (3) enables rapid automated rollback when correctness or performance regressions are detected.

Scope and applicability
----------------------
- Applies to private deployments managed by the Redwood Private control plane and operator-ctl (versions >= 3.4).
- Intended for model-serving pods that use the runtime-service and model-store artifact-buckets mounted via the model-update-controller.
- Not intended for ad-hoc developer testing clusters; use only on customer-managed or Redwood-supported private installs that have telemetry and snapshot hooks enabled.

Key guarantees and SLOs
----------------------
- Atomicity: model-swap is either committed and promoted, or fully rolled back (target success: 99.9% of swaps).
- Minimize downtime: median p95 warm-start latency penalty < 200 ms after swap (measured on per-tenant SLO dashboards).
- Evidence capture latency: forensic artifacts uploaded to evidence-bucket within 60s of swap step completion.
- Retention: evidence artifacts retained for minimum 90 days by default (configurable per-customer).

Primary components referenced
---------------------------
- operator-ctl: field operator tool used to orchestrate transactional swap steps.
- runtime-service: GPU-optimized inference engine handling serving (runs in user tenant pods).
- model-store: artifact store (S3-compatible) for model tarballs and manifests.
- model-update-controller: Kubernetes controller that applies model manifests, supports pre- and post-hooks.
- evidence-bucket: secure, WORM-enabled S3 bucket used for evidence snapshot upload.
- kv-cache-checker: diagnostic binary that validates KV cache compatibility between model revisions.

Preconditions (checklist)
-------------------------
1) Customer preflight: customer has agreed to evidence capture and retention policy and provided an evidence-bucket ARN.
2) Telemetry boundary: control plane has sampling config enabled (trace-level >= info for swap flow).
3) Model artifacts: candidate model tarball and signature (.sig) uploaded to model-store and verified.
4) Baseline health: tenant SLOs green for 24h; no open P0 incidents for serving runtime.
5) Backup snapshot: run automated state snapshot (see 'Snapshot capture' below) and confirm artifact checksum.

High-level flow (phases)
------------------------
1) PREPARE: validate artifacts, coordinate maintenance window, and capture pre-swap evidence.
2) SHADOW: deploy candidate in shadow mode (traffic mirroring) and run smoke & metric comparisons.
3) PROMOTE TRANSACTION: atomically promote candidate via a 3-step commit protocol that includes snapshotting, metadata update, and cache warming.
4) VERIFY: run automated correctness and perf gate checks.
5) FINALIZE OR ROLLBACK: if gates pass, finalize commit and persist evidence; otherwise, trigger automated rollback and forensic dump.

Procedure (detailed)
--------------------
1. PREPARE
   1.1. Notify stakeholders: post to #private-deploy-updates channel, include owner_team and oncall.
   1.2. Lock operator-ctl: operator-ctl lock --tenant <TENANT> --reason "model-swap-YYYYMMDD".
   1.3. Validate candidate: operator-ctl verify-artifact --bucket model-store --key models/my-model/v2.tar.gz --sig models/my-model/v2.tar.gz.sig.
   1.4. Capture pre-swap evidence snapshot:
        - operator-ctl snapshot --type pre-swap --tenant <TENANT> --out /tmp/pre-swap.json
        - Compute checksum: sha256sum /tmp/pre-swap.json -> store in evidence manifest.
   1.5. Upload pre-swap evidence: operator-ctl upload-evidence --file /tmp/pre-swap.json --dest evidence-bucket://<ARN>/tenant/<TENANT>/swaps/<ID>/pre-swap.json

2. SHADOW (traffic mirroring)
   2.1. Deploy candidate in shadow mode (no response path):
        - kubectl apply -f shadow-deployment.yaml --context <CLUSTER>
        shadow-deployment.yaml example:
        apiVersion: apps/v1
        kind: Deployment
        metadata:
          name: my-model-shadow
        spec:
          replicas: 1
          template:
            metadata:
              labels:
                app: runtime-shadow
            spec:
              containers:
              - name: runtime
                image: runtime-service:3.4
                args: ["--model", "s3://model-store/models/my-model/v2.tar.gz", "--shadow"]
   2.2. Enable mirroring: operator-ctl mirror-traffic --from service/my-model --to service/my-model-shadow --rate 100
   2.3. Run comparison harness for N=10k requests or 30 minutes (whichever comes first): operator-ctl run-harness --compare --baseline service/my-model --candidate service/my-model-shadow --metrics latency,error_rate,topk_accuracy
   2.4. Collect shadow metrics and upload: operator-ctl collect-metrics --out /tmp/shadow-metrics.json; operator-ctl upload-evidence --file /tmp/shadow-metrics.json --dest evidence-bucket://<ARN>/tenant/<TENANT>/swaps/<ID>/shadow-metrics.json

3. PROMOTE TRANSACTION (3-step commit)
   Notes: The commit protocol is designed to be idempotent and safe under partial failure. All steps write transaction state to a transaction manifest in model-store and upload a signed checkpoint to evidence-bucket.

   3.1. Step A (Pre-commit): Prepare runtime nodes and warm artifacts
       - operator-ctl precommit --tenant <TENANT> --model-key models/my-model/v2.tar.gz
       - Actions executed by precommit:
         * Pull tarball to node-local model cache (/var/lib/redwood/models/<TENANT>/v2)
         * Validate signature and unpack to read-only path
         * Start warmup containers with --warm-only flag to load KV caches and kernels
       - Expected outputs: /var/lib/redwood/models/<TENANT>/v2/ready = true, uploaded_precommit_checkpoint.json in model-store.

   3.2. Step B (Commit): Switch metadata and lightly quiesce serving traffic
       - operator-ctl commit --tenant <TENANT> --txn <TXN_ID>
       - Actions:
         * Create transaction manifest: models/my-model/transactions/<TXN_ID>.json (includes hex checksum, signer, timestamp)
         * Update control-plane metadata to mark candidate as active in staged config (not fully promoted yet)
         * Signal runtime-service to enter short quiesce window (max 15s) and drain in-flight tokenized requests where safe
       - Evidence: commit_checkpoint.json uploaded to evidence-bucket with operator signature.

   3.3. Step C (Finalize): Flip routing and persist a post-commit snapshot
       - operator-ctl finalize --tenant <TENANT> --txn <TXN_ID>
       - Actions:
         * Update service route to point production endpoint to new model path (atomic label switch)
         * Trigger KV cache canonicalization (kv-cache-checker --canonicalize)
         * Capture post-commit snapshot and upload (post-swap.json)
       - Monitor: watch logs for model-load failures and metric spikes for 10 minutes.

4. VERIFY (automated gates)
   4.1. Gates (all must pass within 10 minutes):
       - Correctness gate: topk_accuracy delta within tolerance (default tolerance 0.5% absolute).
       - Latency gate: p95 latency delta < +15% and absolute p95 < 500 ms.
       - Error gate: 5xx rate does not increase by more than 0.2% absolute.
       - Resource gate: GPU memory < 92% on average per node.
   4.2. Decision: if all gates pass -> FINALIZE (persist evidence and unlock); else -> trigger automatic ROLLBACK.

5. ROLLBACK (if triggered)
   5.1. operator-ctl rollback --tenant <TENANT> --txn <TXN_ID> --reason "gate-failure"
   5.2. Rollback actions:
       - Repoint service route back to previous model manifest.
       - If precommit files were installed, run cleanup hook: operator-ctl cleanup-model --tenant <TENANT> --model-path /var/lib/redwood/models/<TENANT>/v2 --grace 60s
       - Upload rollback evidence bundle with diagnostics: /tmp/rollback-diagnostics.tar.gz -> evidence-bucket.
   5.3. Post-rollback validation: run smoke checks for 5 minutes and ensure SLOs return to baseline.

Snapshot capture and evidence artifacts (required)
------------------------------------------------
All artifacts below must be present for a transaction to be considered auditable. Each artifact is stored under evidence-bucket://<ARN>/tenant/<TENANT>/swaps/<ID>/ and recorded in the transaction manifest.
- pre-swap.json (pre-swap snapshot): runtime graph, model manifest, node versions, control-plane metadata.
- shadow-metrics.json: raw metrics and comparison harness outputs.
- precommit_checkpoint.json, commit_checkpoint.json, postcommit_snapshot.json: signed JSON manifests containing checksums and timestamps.
- kv-cache-delta.json: output of kv-cache-checker showing key diffs, if any.
- logs.tar.gz: concatenated logs from runtime-service, model-update-controller, and operator-ctl for the swap window.
- signatures.asc: operator signatures for each checkpoint.

Artifact retention and legal hold
--------------------------------
- Default retention is 90 days. For customers with legal-hold requirements, set evidence retention policy to 'legal-hold' which marks evidence objects with an extended retention TTL or WORM lock.
- To apply legal hold: operator-ctl evidence-hold --bucket <ARN> --path tenant/<TENANT>/swaps/<ID> --hold true --requested-by <EMAIL>

Automation and integration notes
--------------------------------
- CI/CD: recommended to integrate a pipeline job that runs operator-ctl verify-artifact and pre-run shadow tests on every model artifact push. Example Jenkins snippet:
  stage('Model verify') {
    steps {
      sh \"operator-ctl verify-artifact --bucket model-store --key ${ARTIFACT_KEY} --sig ${SIG_KEY}\"
    }
  }
- Alerting: add these alerts to per-tenant dashboards:
  - swap.gate.failures > 0 -> P1 to oncall
  - swap.evidence.upload.latency > 60s -> P2
  - kv-cache.mismatch > threshold -> P2

Operator runbook (quick commands)
--------------------------------
- Start a transactional swap (example):
  operator-ctl start-swap --tenant acme-corp --model-key models/my-model/v2.tar.gz --evidence-bucket <ARN> --maintenance-window \"2026-03-02T22:00Z/2026-03-02T23:00Z\"
- Force finalize (use only with approval): operator-ctl finalize --tenant acme-corp --txn <TXN_ID> --force --approver "scc@redwood.ai"
- Collect forensic bundle: operator-ctl collect-forensics --tenant acme-corp --txn <TXN_ID> --out /tmp/forensic-bundle.tar.gz

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Primary owner: serving-runtime team (oncall rota: serving-runtime-oncall@redwood.com).
- Evidence retention and legal requests: security-and-compliance team (security@redwood.com).
- Emergency rollback owner: platform-runbook lead (pager: +1-555-0200).
- Escalation path:
  1) Serving-runtime oncall -> 2) Platform runbook lead -> 3) Head of Eng (if SLA breach > 60 mins).

Testing and validation matrix
---------------------------
| Test type | Threshold | Canary size |
|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Functional smoke | 0 failures in 100 requests | 5% traffic mirror |
| Top-k accuracy | delta < 0.5% absolute | 100% mirrored API calls to harness |
| Latency | p95 delta < 15% | 5% production traffic for progressive ramp |

Postmortem and audit checklist
------------------------------
Within 48 hours of any failed swap or rollback:
- Create postmortem in confluence under /incidents/<TENANT>/ with full transaction manifest attached.
- Confirm evidence artifacts exist and checksums verify.
- Conduct RCA with serving-runtime and platform teams and schedule corrective actions.

Appendix: common troubleshooting scenarios
-----------------------------------------
- \"KV cache mismatch on finalization\": run kv-cache-checker --diff --left /var/lib/redwood/models/<TENANT>/v1 --right /var/lib/redwood/models/<TENANT>/v2; if diffs are benign (only ordering), run kv-cache-checker --canonicalize, else rollback.
- \"Evidence upload failed (timeout)\": check network egress ACLs toward evidence-bucket and re-run operator-ctl upload-evidence --retry 5 --backoff 30s.
- \"Shadow harness shows functional drift (>5%)\": abort swap immediately and collect artifacts (operator-ctl collect-forensics).

Related documents
-----------------
- See upgrade-and-rollback/private-deploy-evidence-preservation-and-forensic-playbook for legal templates and retention mappings.
- See day-2-ops/kv-cache-consistency-chaos-validation-and-rollback-matrix for chaos test patterns used by the shadow harness.
